coupling: The defect is split across two real commits that both touch the same overflow-hardening theme. (1) 68c0d81 'Fix integer multiplication overflows' adds a new shared constant MATIO_MAX_EDGE_PRODUCT (defined in matio_private.h as SIZE_MAX / sizeof(matvar_t *), i.e. 'however many pointer-sized elements could ever be allocated') and uses it in mcos.c's ResolveEncodedMCOS to bound an object count that is only ever used as a size_t allocation/loop count there - a safe, correct use of a loose bound. (2) 615f77f 'Validate edge product in Mat_VarGetCells and Mat_VarGetStructs' adds CheckEdgeOverflow() and, in my edit, makes it compare the validated edge-product against this same shared MATIO_MAX_EDGE_PRODUCT constant instead of a hardcoded (size_t)INT_MAX (with its own '#if !defined' fallback to INT_MAX so the function still compiles and is safe if the shared constant is never defined). Neither edit is unsafe by itself: with only (1) applied, CheckEdgeOverflow still falls back to its local INT_MAX definition (the macro from matio_private.h is never consulted because 615f77f's own code is unedited and uses the literal (size_t)INT_MAX directly), so Mat_VarGetCells' 32-bit `int N` element count stays correctly bounded. With only (2) applied, matio_private.h never defines MATIO_MAX_EDGE_PRODUCT, so CheckEdgeOverflow's own '#if !defined' guard defines it locally as the historical (size_t)INT_MAX, which is again safe. Only when BOTH edits are present does matio_private.h's loose, size_t-only-correct bound (defined for mcos.c's legitimate use) get silently inherited by CheckEdgeOverflow's guard (already defined by the time mat.c is compiled), raising the effective bound from ~2^31 to ~2^61. Mat_VarGetCells (src/matvar_cell.c) still narrows the validated edge product into a 32-bit `int N` used both to size the output malloc and to bound the write loop, so an edge product between 2^32 and the new loose bound silently truncates to a small N (undersized malloc) while the inner loop still iterates edge[0] times, writing past the undersized buffer. A correct fix requires reasoning about both commits together: fixing only (1) (e.g. tightening mcos.c's own bound) leaves CheckEdgeOverflow's edited comparison against the still-loose shared constant; fixing only (2) (e.g. restoring the literal (size_t)INT_MAX in CheckEdgeOverflow) leaves the shared constant itself loose and mcos.c's use of it unaffected either way - the bug only disappears when the shared constant is tightened back to INT_MAX-scale AND/OR CheckEdgeOverflow stops deferring to it, i.e. when both edits are reverted (verified: reverting either edit alone while keeping the other makes the PoC pass cleanly; keeping both reproduces the heap-buffer-overflow).
